existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `ImmunizationRecommendation` appears to have been removed from R6 core, which is a hard R4→R6 break. The top migration concerns are loss of the `resourceType`, loss of the local forecasting content model including modifier `forecastStatus`, and lack of an official replacement/map. The main uncertainty is standards intent: the local package proves absence but not the recommended R6 migration pattern.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Treat R4 `ImmunizationRecommendation` as a discontinued resource unless an external IG or official cross-version map says otherwise. Migration will likely need a policy choice: keep R4 payloads at a boundary, map selected content into profiled R6 workflow resources plus extensions, or preserve complete forecast snapshots in a custom extension/contained artifact. A simple path rename is not available.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the resource is absent from the checked R6 ballot package because the assigned file is missing, package indexes and exact text searches found no `ImmunizationRecommendation`, and R6 type code systems list `Immunization` but not `ImmunizationRecommendation`. Confidence is lower for the best migration target because no official diff, narrative rationale, or ConceptMap was available locally.

rationaleMd:
ImmunizationRecommendation has a resource-identity break: ImmunizationRecommendation resource is absent from the R6 ballot core package. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 1, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 93/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

1 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
